cover.title: 5 niche ways to turn rage clicks into revenue

inner.title: set the 3-click rule
inner.body: amplitude says tools usually flag a rage click as 3+ clicks on one target within about 2 seconds. if you never filter for it, your angriest visitors look like every other session.

inner.title: hunt the ghost buttons
inner.body: inspectlet lists elements that look clickable but aren't as a top cause: unlinked images, cards with one tiny inner link. your buyer is trying to pay you and the design says nothing.

inner.title: answer in 100 milliseconds
inner.body: inspectlet recommends feedback within about 100ms: a spinner, a disabled button, a progress bar. it also lists debouncing duplicate submissions, because a shopper who gets silence clicks pay twice.

inner.title: match clicks to errors
inner.body: inspectlet traces rage clicks to broken javascript: unhandled promise rejections, third-party script conflicts, silent cors failures. the click isn't the bug, and your users find the error before you do.

inner.title: fix the top three
inner.body: inspectlet calls rage clicks on 5%+ of sessions for one element critical, and under 1% worth watching. it claims fixing the top 3 hotspots lifts conversion 5 to 15%, from its own experience, not a study.
